items.title: Lillie Delk Christian Interview, 1961-04-25
items.q: Some of those people, now like Ethel Waters, she would mix hers.

ctx.x: Let's see. That's kind of hard to figure out because in fact, they've been, it seemed like the blues was most popular, you know, for the records. and when my kind of singing came out it was something unusual, you know, and then the people seemed to like it, see, it was most unusual because the average one was singing blues, see. So now I can't
recall just who the popular singers were. Some of those people, now like Ethel Waters, she would mix hers. You know, she'd sing blue melody number, then

she'd sing swing number, you know, something like that. Well, would Florence Mills be regarded as a... she was a show singer, wasn't she? Yeah. Mainly a popular... I tried. Yeah, you wouldn't class her as a blue singer. No. No. And still, you weren't doing musical comedies, so you weren't exactly that same category either way.
